name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
insider_take: The Carlyle isn't just a hotel — it's a living piece of New York legend, where old-world glamour meets Upper East Side sophistication at its absolute finest.
whats_special: A true Manhattan institution since 1930, The Carlyle has hosted every U.S. president since Truman, earning its nickname "The President's New York Home." Home to Bemelmans Bar , the only remaining New York City bar still adorned with original murals painted by Ludwig Bemelmans — the beloved creator of Madeline — who paid for his suite by decorating the walls. The legendary Café Carlyle has hosted icons like Woody Allen, Eartha Kitt, and Bobby Short, making it one of NYC's most storied cabaret venues. Perched on 76th & Madison Avenue, guests enjoy direct access to Museum Mile, Central Park, and the world's finest luxury boutiques.
pro_tip: Reserve a seat at Bemelmans Bar on a weeknight for live jazz in an intimate setting — arrive early, as this iconic spot fills fast. Order the house cocktail and soak in those one-of-a-kind murals.
dont_miss: Central Park — just one block away, perfect for a morning stroll or a horse-drawn carriage ride. The Metropolitan Museum of Art — steps from the hotel along the iconic Museum Mile on Fifth Avenue. Gallery Row on Madison Avenue — world-class art galleries right at your doorstep. Café Carlyle — catch a live cabaret performance for an unforgettable New York night out.
pros: Iconic Upper East Side location with timeless New York elegance
World-renowned Café Carlyle with legendary jazz performances
Exceptional white-glove service and personalized attention
Luxurious residential-style suites with Central Park proximity
cons: Premium pricing reflects exclusive Manhattan location
Traditional formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers
